outstandingFindings.summary: No feature flag is declared. A cutover that replaces live navigation and widens natural-language reach warrants a flag, but G111 requires an introduced flag to be default-OFF in every non-owning train's bundle, which requires editing config/feature-flags.mvp.yaml — owned by bubbles.train and outside this run's permitted surface. flagsIntroduced is deliberately empty rather than falsely populated.

R-112-23 through R-112-26 depend on spec 108's corpus:read grant model. Spec 108 is specs_hardened — planned, not delivered — and targets the same 'next' train. Surfacing capabilities before that boundary is enforceable violates policy P4 (reach never outruns the guard). SCOPE-03 and everything downstream of it cannot execute first.

The registry's unit is the capability; the built artifacts are prompt contracts, and the mapping is not 1:1 — 17 of 27 contracts carry a routable id, 10 are pipeline stages that carry none. The rule that decides what constitutes one capability, and how contracts bind to capabilities, is undecided. Getting it wrong reproduces the original duplication at a new granularity.

R-112-31 requires the coverage check to compare against an independently derived universe of built capabilities. How that universe is derived — and how it avoids the circularity already present at tests/integration/experience/route_inventory_test.go:92-100, where the expected set is built from the catalog under validation — is undecided. Without this the check cannot fail and is decorative.

Spec 109 explicitly forbids deriving the MCP tool list by passthrough from agent.All(). The external tool projection must therefore be a per-capability declared projection, not a blanket export of the capability set. Reconciling R-112-08 with that constraint is a design decision.

Three navigation authorities are live and already divergent, and internal/experience/catalog.go:10 records that their cutover was deferred to a later scope of the shell specification. Whether this feature performs that cutover or hands it to the shell spec is undecided, and R-112-09 cannot be satisfied by whichever spec does not.

The slash alias table and the assistant registry currently contradict each other on /ask, /recipe and /cook. Generating both from one descriptor forces a decision about which existing behaviour is correct. That decision changes shipped user-visible behaviour for at least one token and cannot be made silently by a generator.

29 of 31 first-party PWA pages render no shared navigation. R-112-20 is satisfiable in principle by a core that reaches only surfaces which render navigation at all, which would make the guarantee vacuous on most pages. The relationship between this feature's guarantee and the island pages must be stated rather than assumed.

The authoring brief noted that .specify/templates/spec-template.md is expected to govern spec structure; that file does not exist in this repository (.specify/ contains only memory/, metrics/ and runtime/). spec.md follows the adjacent sibling spec's structure and the Bubbles BDD scenario contract instead. Either the template should be installed or the instruction corrected.

Observed while reading siblings for consistency and NOT modified here, because that spec is outside this run's permitted surface. Recorded because gate G110 covers train declaration across specs.

executionHistory.summary: Authored spec.md for one capability registry projecting to every reachability surface, from diagnostic findings D17 and D18, governed by Pillar C of docs/Product_Delivery_Plan.md. Produced a domain capability model with 9 binding policies, 5 actors, 5 use cases, 26 Gherkin scenarios with stable SCN-112-* ids across five groups (one record many projections, declared exposure, guaranteed navigation core, authorization, coverage check), 33 requirements, 6 non-functional requirements, 7 non-goals, 10 routed findings, product principle alignment, release-train declaration, and an exposure contract. Zero source files changed, zero tests executed, zero DoD boxes checked.
executionHistory.sourceVerification: Every claim in the authoring brief was re-read against the working tree before being written into spec.md, and all hold. 27 contracts confirmed in config/prompt_contracts/; exactly 5 user_facing: true confirmed at config/assistant/scenarios.yaml:26,34,42,56,72 with the five named ids matching; 31 first-party PWA pages confirmed with exactly 2 (assistant.html, index.html) loading web/pwa/lib/appnav.js; internal/experience/ confirmed to contain catalog.gen.json with 20 surfaces under schema smackerel-product-experience/v1 plus navigation_projection.go, renderer_projection.go, consumer_inventory.go, state and mutation presenters and validator.go. TWO FACTS WERE FOUND THAT THE BRIEF DID NOT STATE, BOTH STRENGTHENING IT. First, the capability reference already exists and points at nothing: every catalog surface carries a capability_id and validator.go:99 already emits an unknown-capability violation, but no capability record exists anywhere — in config/smackerel.yaml capability_id appears only as a surface attribute (:2706-2934) with no capabilities: block, and the only production-shaped test supplies the universe via iCapsOf(cat) at tests/integration/experience/route_inventory_test.go:92-100, deriving the expected set from the catalog under validation so the check is circular and cannot fail. Second, the predicted drift is already real and was demonstrated with three live contradictions: web/pwa/lib/appnav.js:22 asserts it mirrors internal/web/appshell.go:31 but the two have diverged (capture/connectors/photos PWA-only, knowledge server-only); internal/assistant/shortcuts.go:47 maps /ask to open_knowledge while config/assistant/scenarios.yaml:25-31 assigns /ask to retrieval_qa; and shortcuts.go:50-51 ships /recipe and /cook while scenarios.yaml records recipe_search with an empty shortcut and a comment that the set is frozen without them.
executionHistory.claimSharpened: THE BRIEF'S FIGURE OF 22 UNSURFACED CAPABILITIES WAS NARROWED TO 11 ON EVIDENCE, NOT ACCEPTED AS GIVEN. D17 and the plan of record both reach 22 as 27 minus 5; the arithmetic is correct but the units are mixed, because a prompt contract is not a capability. Ten of the 27 contracts declare a pipeline type (domain-extraction x3, query-augment, lint-audit, ingest-synthesis, drive-folder-context, drive-classification, digest-assembly, cross-source-connection) and carry no routable id: at all — they are invoked directly by their owning service and were never dispatchable. One more, e2e_ollama_smoke, is a test harness by its own description. Only the 17 contracts declaring type: scenario carry a routable id. The genuinely unsurfaced dispatchable set is therefore 11: alert_timing_evaluate, annotation_classify, expertise_classify, hospitality_concern_evaluate, recommendation_feedback, recommendation_reactive, recommendation_watch_evaluate, recommendation_why, relationship_cooling_evaluate, resurface_evaluate, retrieval_evergreen. This narrows the count and strengthens the finding: the real defect is that the repository cannot tell you which number is right, because nothing records whether a contract is unsurfaced deliberately or by omission. D18 was likewise held to its stated scope — a core-membership finding, not an unreachability claim — because internal/web/templates.go:79-84 appends the digest link after including the shared partial, so the digest IS reachable in the server shell while absent from the shared core.

executionHistory.releaseTrainRationale: Chose 'next' (target_slot staging) over 'mvp' (target_slot home-lab) on four grounds. (1) This feature RAISES REACH while the guard that should bound it is not delivered: surfacing the eleven currently-undeclared dispatchable capabilities makes them invocable by anyone who can talk to the assistant, and the per-capability authorization that bounds that — spec 108's corpus:read — is specs_hardened, not delivered, and targets 'next'. Shipping the exposure on the live train while its boundary lives on the other train is exactly what policy P4 forbids. (2) Both hard dependencies are on 'next': spec 108 (grants) and spec 109 (external tool surface) are both specs_hardened there, so a registry on 'mvp' would project into a tool list that does not exist on that train and declare grants that train does not enforce. (3) It replaces three live and already-divergent navigation authorities on a running shell, which is a change with real regression surface on every page a user touches; proving it on staging first is the correct order. (4) The sibling precedent is consistent — spec 111 chose 'next' on the same reasoning, and spec 108 states in its own words that a security-posture change MUST NOT ship on mvp. The honest cost of this choice — that the mvp train keeps the D17/D18 reachability gap for longer — is stated explicitly in spec.md rather than obscured by the train choice.
